items.content_html:
proxmox.qemuConf.diskSize is a compatibility alias for virtualisation.diskSize. Serializing all of qemuConf evaluates the alias and emits a deprecation warning even when users did not configure the old option.

This warning was previously fixed in ae027401. The later Proxmox cloud-image refactor in #429178 reintroduced serialization of the full qemuConf set.

Exclude only the compatibility alias from the generated qemu-server.conf. Image sizing continues to use virtualisation.diskSize. Explicit use of the deprecated option still warns and maps to the new option, and an explicit qemuExtraConf.diskSize value remains supported.

Testing

Native Proxmox image evaluations verified that:

  • the default configuration evaluates without the deprecation warning
  • proxmox.qemuConf.diskSize = 2048 still warns and produces virtualisation.diskSize = 2048
  • proxmox.qemuExtraConf.diskSize = 4096 remains present in the generated QEMU configuration
  • the changed file passes nixfmt

Automation disclosure: OpenCode (OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol) assisted with tracing the regression, preparing the patch and PR text, running the evaluation checks, and a second-pass review. I reviewed the patch and test results.

When useBootLoader, useDefaultFilesystems and systemd-boot are used build an image holding only the ESP instead of a full system disk image.

Previously whenever useBootLoader was set it would cause a full disk image to be built, when in reality, all that was needed for the test was having a real bootloader.

A full system disk image embeds the whole closure, so it is about 1.3 GB and rebuilds on any closure change. The ESP image is 44 MB and changes only with the kernel, initrd or boot loader. Across the systemd-boot tests this drops the built images from roughly 32 GB to 1.1 GB.

  • Tested on my systemd nightly (v262) CI on x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux.
  • Tested on all tests in nixpkgs which would be affected (useBootLoader && useDefaultFilesystems && systemd-boot.enable) on x86_64-linux.

Fixes: #489197

Qemu is moving to a new way of doing UEFI var storage:
Context:

  • https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/devel/uefi-vars.html
  • https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/edk2/-/blob/master/OvmfPkg/QEMU_PV_VARS.md
  • https://gitlab.com/kraxel/virt-firmware-rs/-/blob/main/varstore/README.md?ref_type=heads

This attempts to do so, but the build hangs on aarch64-linux.

I suspect this is because of the edk2-var-generator usage inside the derivation:

  1. It shouldn't be necessary, if we move to the json var storage.
  2. It's... vastly overkill. virt-firmware has a python script that can do this, seemingly without running qemu...

So this is a draft, because there's more work/consideration that needs to happen, hopefully from EDK2/OVMF/qemu maintainers.

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds virtualisation.bootDiskAdditionalSpace option to configure additional disk space beyond the NixOS closure when useBootLoader = true.

Problem

When virtualisation.useBootLoader = true, qemu-vm.nix creates a systemImage via make-disk-image.nix with additionalSpace = "0M" hardcoded. This means the backing disk image is sized exactly to fit the NixOS closure with zero free space.

Consequence: Any runtime writes fail with ENOSPC (no space left on device):

  • NixOS integration tests that write runtime data
  • Container runtimes pulling images (Docker, Podman)
  • Databases writing journals or data files
  • Applications creating logs or temporary files

The existing virtualisation.diskSize only controls the qcow2 overlay size, not the backing systemImage. This distinction is subtle and undocumented, leading users to expect diskSize to control total available space.

Related Context

The pattern of needing configurable disk space is well-established:

  • VirtualBox module exposes virtualisation.virtualbox.guest.baseImageFreeSpace for the same purpose
  • make-disk-image.nix defaults to additionalSpace = "512M", suggesting this headroom is expected—qemu-vm.nix overriding to "0M" appears unintentional

Changes

  • New option: virtualisation.bootDiskAdditionalSpace (type: string, default: "512M")
  • Wiring: Passes configured value to make-disk-image.nix additionalSpace parameter
  • Test: New qemu-vm-bootdisk-space test validating the option works

Test plan

  • Existing nixosTests.systemd-boot.basic passes
  • New nixosTests.qemu-vm-bootdisk-space passes (tests default 512M, custom 1G, minimal 64M configurations)

Notes for reviewers

Behavioral change: Default increases from "0M" to "512M" additional space. This matches make-disk-image.nix's own default and provides reasonable headroom. Users wanting the old behavior can set bootDiskAdditionalSpace = "0M".

Why a new option vs. respecting diskSize? The existing virtualisation.diskSize controls the qcow2 overlay size, not the backing systemImage. Overloading it would conflate two distinct concepts. A dedicated option is clearer and doesn't change overlay behavior.

items.content_html:
The qemu-vm.nix module gets a new mountHostNixStoreClosureOnly option.
The option mounts the user's host store with a lightweight projection (a "sub-store") of the VM closure, providing both great performance and correct security/privacy.

There are currently three ways to configure how the VM store is built:

  • mountHostNixStore (default): Mounts the store via 9p. Fast, but exposes the whole host store inside the VM.
  • useNixStoreImage: Builds an erofs image at runtime. Slower at runtime, but exposes only the closure of the VM.
  • useBootLoader: Builds a full qcow2 image with the closure inside it. Slowest at build time, exposes only the closure of the VM, duplicates the closure inside the qcow2 image, and thus into the store.

This PR proposes a fourth way, by combining both mountHostNixStore and (the new) mountHostNixStoreClosureOnly option. This method is fast, exposes only the closure of the VM inside the guest and does not store anything else into the store. In practice, this is implemented by wrapping the virtiofsd daemon through a light binary nix-substore over an unshared mount and user namespace. The binary reads the closure of the VM from a file built with pkgs.closureInfo and bind-mounts each store path into a tmpdir, which is the new so-called sub-store. The overhead consists only of O(n) calls to the mount syscall.

In an effort to standardize the way sharedDirectories are implemented, this PR moves all the sharedDirectories from 9p to virtiofsd. virtiofsd is "much faster" than 9p. However, virtiofsd does not implement the mapped-xattr and mapped-file security modes that 9p provides. In the current implementation, the only option for affected users would be to re-implement the shared directories themselves by using qemu.options and fileSystems.

If we cannot reach a consensus that the securityMode of 9p can be ignored in this re-implementation of the shared directories, I am open to supporting both 9p and virtiofsd and making the modifications required to support both.

As a side note, I would like to point out that, in the future, NixOS containers could be modified to also use the nix-substore binary (responsible for setting up the sub-stores) and expose only the closure of the container instead of the whole store.
